+package strategy
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"log/slog"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
+)
+
+// CheckpointReadRemotes returns the ordered, deduped remotes that checkpoint
+// READS consult: the elected sync remote first, then "origin" as the legacy
+// tier (pre-single-remote-sync checkpoints live there, and a fresh clone
+// may lack the local settings that elected a non-origin remote).
+//
+// Unlike the write-side election, this fails OPEN: on an election error
+// (misconfigured checkpoint_push_remote, unreadable settings) the chain is
+// ["origin"] when configured. Writes fail closed to prevent leaking data;
+// failing reads closed would only prevent FINDING data, with no privacy
+// benefit. Callers must uphold the read-only rule for every candidate after
+// the first: only the elected remote may seed or advance local refs.
+//
+// An empty result means no candidates — callers needing the "checkpoint
+// absent" classification must gather their own positive evidence (successful
+// remote listing, readable settings); an empty chain alone is not proof.
+//
+// Deliberately un-memoized: every call re-runs the election (~2 git
+// subprocesses plus a settings.Load). Callers on hot paths (per-turn hooks,
+// checkpoint.Open sites) accept that cost for always-fresh results; revisit
+// with memoization only if profiling shows it matters.
+func CheckpointReadRemotes(ctx context.Context) []string {
+	return CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection(ctx).Candidates
+}
+
+// CheckpointReadResolution is the read-candidate chain bundled with the
+// election result it was derived from.
+type CheckpointReadResolution struct {
+	// Candidates is the ordered read-candidate chain (see
+	// CheckpointReadRemotes).
+	Candidates []string
+	// ElectedName is the elected checkpoint sync remote; "" when the election
+	// failed or elected nothing. Only this remote may seed or advance local
+	// refs.
+	ElectedName string
+	// ElectionErr records a failed election. It is advisory for readers (the
+	// chain fail-opens to ["origin"] when configured); write-adjacent callers
+	// may surface it when they need a push target.
+	ElectionErr error
+}
+
+// CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection returns the read-candidate chain together
+// with the election result it was derived from, so callers that need both —
+// e.g. to confine local-ref advancement to the elected remote while iterating
+// the chain — make ONE election call instead of two that could disagree if
+// settings or remotes change mid-operation. See CheckpointReadRemotes for the
+// read-side fail-open rationale and cost note.
+func CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection(ctx context.Context) CheckpointReadResolution {
+	var res CheckpointReadResolution
+	elected, err := ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote(ctx)
+	switch {
+	case err != nil:
+		res.ElectionErr = err
+		logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoint reads: election failed, falling back to origin only",
+			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
+	case elected.Name != "":
+		res.ElectedName = elected.Name
+		res.Candidates = append(res.Candidates, elected.Name)
+	}
+	if isConfiguredRemote(ctx, "origin") && (len(res.Candidates) == 0 || res.Candidates[0] != "origin") {
+		res.Candidates = append(res.Candidates, "origin")
+	}
+	return res
+}

31	// data is fetched from. It prefers the effective URL resolved by FetchURL,
32	// which is the source of truth for checkpoint fetch location. If URL
33	// resolution fails, it falls back to the origin remote name so callers can
34	// still attempt a fetch.
35	func CheckpointFetchTarget(ctx context.Context) string {
36		target, _ := checkpointFetchTarget(ctx)
37		return target
38	}

40	// checkpointFetchTarget is CheckpointFetchTarget plus whether the target is
41	// authoritative for checkpoint refs (see fetchURLAuthoritative). A resolved
42	// origin is also non-authoritative when checkpoint_push_remote elects another
43	// remote: it may still be probed as a fallback, but cannot certify absence.
44	func checkpointFetchTarget(ctx context.Context) (string, bool) {
45		target, authoritative := checkpointFetchTargetFrom(ctx, "")
46		if !authoritative {
47			return target, false
48		}
49	
50		s, err := settings.Load(ctx)
51		if err != nil {
52			return target, false
53		}
54		if s.HasCheckpointRemoteKey() {
55			return target, s.GetCheckpointRemote() != nil
56		}
57	
58		pushRemote := s.GetCheckpointPushRemote()
59		return target, pushRemote == "" || pushRemote == originRemote
60	}
61	
62	func checkpointFetchTargetFrom(ctx context.Context, leadRemote string) (string, bool) {
63		url, authoritative, err := fetchURLAuthoritative(ctx, FetchURLOptions{LeadReadRemote: leadRemote})
64		if err == nil && url != "" {
65			return url, authoritative
66		}
67		if leadRemote != "" {
68			return leadRemote, false
69		}
70		return "origin", false
71	}
72	
73	// FetchCheckpointRef fetches a single per-checkpoint ref
74	// (refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) from the checkpoint remote into the
75	// local ref of the same name, so the git-refs store can resolve a checkpoint
76	// written on another machine.
77	//
78	// Contract — absence is distinguishable from failure:
79	//   - The remote genuinely lacking the ref returns an error wrapping
80	//     plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound (probed via ls-remote before fetching,
81	//     because `git fetch` of a missing refspec fails indistinguishably from a
82	//     transport error). Store probes classify this as "checkpoint not found",
83	//     which write routing may legitimately act on.
84	//   - Any transport-level failure (probe or fetch) is surfaced as a real
85	//     error, never mapped to absence — a false "absent" would misdirect a
86	//     backfill onto another backend instead of retrying.
87	//   - A repository with no git remotes at all and no checkpoint_remote
88	//     configured also returns an error wrapping plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound
89	//     without probing: there is no remote that could host the ref.
90	func FetchCheckpointRef(ctx context.Context, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
91		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, readFetchTimeout)
92		defer cancel()
93	
94		fetchTarget, authoritative := checkpointFetchTarget(ctx)
95	
96		// A fully local repository — no git remotes at all and no
97		// checkpoint_remote configured — has no remote that could host checkpoint
98		// refs, so the ref's local absence is the final verdict. Without this,
99		// the origin-name fallback below probes a remote git cannot resolve
100		// ("'origin' does not appear to be a git repository", exit 128) and a
101		// remoteless repo is misreported as a transport outage. Absence is only
102		// ever classified on positive evidence; each escape below keeps today's
103		// hard-failure probe:
104		//   - dead caller context: every subprocess fails for reasons that say
105		//     nothing about the repository
106		//   - unreadable settings: a configured checkpoint remote cannot be
107		//     ruled out
108		//   - checkpoint_remote key present in any form, valid or malformed
109		//     (see settings.HasCheckpointRemoteKey for why key presence, not
110		//     GetCheckpointRemote, is the signal)
111		//   - any remote listed, or the listing itself failing: checkpoint refs
112		//     are pushed to whatever remote the pre-push hook fires for, so a
113		//     repo with only non-origin remotes is NOT remoteless
114		// The skipped-guard cases surface through the ordinary probe paths: a
115		// missing origin fails the ls-remote probe as a transport error, and an
116		// origin that merely lacks the ref hits the fallback-emptiness refusal
117		// below — neither classifies as absence.
118		if fetchTarget == originRemote && !authoritative && ctx.Err() == nil {
119			s, loadErr := settings.Load(ctx)
120			switch {
121			case loadErr != nil:
122				logging.Warn(ctx, "checkpoint probe: settings unreadable; cannot rule out a configured checkpoint remote, probing anyway",
123					slog.String("error", loadErr.Error()))
124			case !s.HasCheckpointRemoteKey() && repoHasNoRemotes(ctx):
125				logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoint probe: repository has no git remotes; classifying ref as absent",
126					slog.String("ref", ref.String()))
127				return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint ref %s: repository has no git remotes to fetch from: %w", ref, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound)
128			}
129		}
130	
131		return probeAndFetchCheckpointRef(ctx, ref, fetchTarget, authoritative)
132	}
133	
134	// FetchCheckpointRefFrom fetches a checkpoint ref from an ordered read chain.
135	// Candidates advance only after positive absence. A transport failure stops
136	// the chain because hydrating a legacy ref into the canonical local ref while
137	// the elected remote is unavailable could make stale data shadow the elected
138	// copy. A configured checkpoint_remote keeps the existing single-target
139	// behavior.
140	//
141	// The readFetchTimeout bounds the complete chain, not each candidate. When
142	// electionErr is non-nil, the fail-open origin candidate may still satisfy a
143	// read, but its emptiness cannot certify global absence.
144	func FetchCheckpointRefFrom(ctx context.Context, ref plumbing.ReferenceName, readRemotes []string, electionErr error) error {
145		s, loadErr := settings.Load(ctx)
146		if loadErr != nil || s.HasCheckpointRemoteKey() {
147			return FetchCheckpointRef(ctx, ref)
148		}
149	
150		chainCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, readFetchTimeout)
151		defer cancel()
152	
153		if len(readRemotes) == 0 {
154			if electionErr != nil {
155				return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint ref %s: checkpoint remote election failed; no authoritative read candidate is available: %w", ref, electionErr)
156			}
157			if chainCtx.Err() == nil && !s.HasCheckpointRemoteKey() && repoHasNoRemotes(chainCtx) {
158				logging.Debug(chainCtx, "checkpoint probe: repository has no git remotes; classifying ref as absent",
159					slog.String("ref", ref.String()))
160				return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint ref %s: repository has no git remotes to fetch from: %w", ref, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound)
161			}
162			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint ref %s: no checkpoint read candidates available and the repository is not provably remoteless; refusing to treat this as absence", ref)
163		}
164	
165		var firstErr error
166		for i, remoteName := range readRemotes {
167			target, authoritative := checkpointFetchTargetFrom(chainCtx, remoteName)
168			var err error
169			if !authoritative {
170				err = fmt.Errorf("resolve checkpoint read candidate %q: resolved target %s is not authoritative", remoteName, RedactURLOrPath(target))
171			} else {
172				err = probeAndFetchCheckpointRef(chainCtx, ref, target, true)
173			}
174			if err == nil {
175				return nil
176			}
177			if firstErr == nil {
178				firstErr = err
179			}
180			if !errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
181				return err
182			}
183			if i+1 < len(readRemotes) {
184				logging.Debug(ctx, "checkpoint ref fetch: read candidate failed; trying next candidate",
185					slog.String("ref", ref.String()),
186					slog.String("candidate", remoteName),
187					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
188			}
189		}
190		if electionErr != nil && errors.Is(firstErr, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
191			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint ref %s: checkpoint remote election failed; origin fallback cannot certify absence: %w", ref, electionErr)
192		}
193		return firstErr
194	}
195	
196	func probeAndFetchCheckpointRef(ctx context.Context, ref plumbing.ReferenceName, fetchTarget string, authoritative bool) error {
197		out, err := LsRemoteInDir(ctx, "", fetchTarget, ref.String())
198		if err != nil {
199			// Redact: fetchTarget can be a remote URL with embedded credentials
200			// (CI origin URLs), and this error is logged and shown to users.
201			return fmt.Errorf("probe checkpoint ref %s on %s: %w", ref, RedactURLOrPath(fetchTarget), err)
202		}
203		if len(bytes.TrimSpace(out)) == 0 {
204			if !authoritative {
205				// The probe hit an origin FALLBACK while a checkpoint_remote is
206				// configured (or undeterminable) — a remote that may simply never
207				// host the configured checkpoint refs. Emptiness there proves
208				// nothing; classifying it as absence would silently drop backfills
209				// for checkpoints that exist on the real checkpoint remote.
210				return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint ref %s not visible on fallback remote %s, and the configured checkpoint remote could not be resolved; refusing to treat this as absence", ref, RedactURLOrPath(fetchTarget))
211			}
212			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint ref %s not found on %s: %w", ref, RedactURLOrPath(fetchTarget), plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound)
213		}
214	
215		refSpec := "+" + ref.String() + ":" + ref.String()
216		if fetchOut, err := Fetch(ctx, FetchOptions{
217			Remote:   fetchTarget,
218			RefSpecs: []string{refSpec},
219			NoTags:   true,
220		}); err != nil {
221			// Fold git's own output into the error (redacted): a bare
222			// "exit status 128" is undebuggable in hook Warn logs.
223			msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(fetchOut))
224			safeTarget := RedactURLOrPath(fetchTarget)
225			msg = strings.ReplaceAll(msg, fetchTarget, safeTarget)
226			if msg != "" {
227				return fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s from %s: %s: %w", ref, safeTarget, msg, err)
228			}
229			return fmt.Errorf("fetch checkpoint ref %s from %s: %w", ref, safeTarget, err)
230		}
231		return nil
232	}
233	
234	// repoHasNoRemotes reports whether the repository at the current directory
235	// definitively has no git remotes configured. Only a successful, empty
236	// `git remote` listing counts as proof; any error (dead context, missing git
237	// binary, not a repository) returns false so the caller falls through to the
238	// probe instead of classifying absence off an undifferentiated failure.
239	func repoHasNoRemotes(ctx context.Context) bool {
240		out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote").Output()
241		return err == nil && len(bytes.TrimSpace(out)) == 0
242	}
243	
244	// HookCheckpointRefFetcher returns the write-probe fetcher for git-hook
245	// contexts (post-commit attribution, stop-time transcript finalize): the
246	// bounded budget plus BatchMode SSH, so a passphrase-protected key can never
247	// prompt — or invisibly hang — inside a hook the user's git command is
248	// waiting on.
249	//
250	// This remains single-target because write-side probes must not broaden their
251	// destination beyond the remote selected by the push flow.
252	func HookCheckpointRefFetcher() func(context.Context, plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
253		bounded := BoundedCheckpointRefFetcher(WriteProbeFetchBudget)
254		return func(ctx context.Context, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
255			return bounded(WithNonInteractiveSSH(ctx), ref)
256		}
257	}
258	
259	// BoundedCheckpointRefFetcher returns a RefFetchFunc-shaped fetcher whose
260	// per-call budget is capped at d, for wiring into write-path checkpoint
261	// stores (see WriteProbeFetchBudget).
262	func BoundedCheckpointRefFetcher(d time.Duration) func(context.Context, plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
263		return func(ctx context.Context, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
264			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, d)
265			defer cancel()
266			return FetchCheckpointRef(ctx, ref)
267		}
268	}

+	)

+

+			env.CheckpointStore = StoreGitRefs

+			if checkpointRemote == upstreamRemote {
+				env.PatchSettings(map[string]any{
+					"strategy_options": map[string]any{
+						"checkpoint_push_remote": upstreamRemote,
+					},
+				})
+			}
+
+			checkpointID := createCheckpointedCommit(t, env, "Add machine module", "machine.go", "package machine", "Add machine module")
+			env.GitPush(originRemote, "HEAD")
+			env.RunPrePush(checkpointRemote)
+
+			bareByRemote := map[string]string{originRemote: bareOrigin, upstreamRemote: bareUpstream}
+			if !env.CheckpointExistsOnRemote(bareByRemote[checkpointRemote], checkpointID) {
+				t.Fatalf("checkpoint %s should be on %s", checkpointID, checkpointRemote)
+			}
+			otherRemote := originRemote
+			if checkpointRemote == originRemote {
+				otherRemote = upstreamRemote
+			}
+			if env.CheckpointExistsOnRemote(bareByRemote[otherRemote], checkpointID) {
+				t.Fatalf("fixture: checkpoint %s must exist only on %s", checkpointID, checkpointRemote)
+			}
+
+			// Machine B always elects upstream. The origin case therefore proves
+			// that a miss on the elected remote advances to the legacy tier.
+			cloneEnv := env.CloneFrom(bareOrigin)
+			testutil.AddRemote(t, cloneEnv.RepoDir, upstreamRemote, bareUpstream)
+			cloneEnv.setGitConfigBaseline()
+			cloneEnv.PatchSettings(map[string]any{
+				"strategy_options": map[string]any{
+					"checkpoint_push_remote": upstreamRemote,
+				},
+			})
+			if cloneEnv.CheckpointsPresentLocally() {
+				t.Fatal("fixture: the clone must start with zero local checkpoint state")
+			}
+
+			listOutput := cloneEnv.RunCLI("checkpoint", "list")
+			if !strings.Contains(listOutput, "Add machine module") && !strings.Contains(listOutput, checkpointID[:8]) {
+				t.Errorf("cross-machine discovery should surface the remote checkpoint, got:\n%s", listOutput)
+			}
+
+			output := cloneEnv.RunCLI("checkpoint", "explain", "--checkpoint", checkpointID)
+			if !strings.Contains(output, "Add machine module") {
+				t.Errorf("the discovered checkpoint should hydrate on read, got:\n%s", output)
+			}
+		})
+	}
